lines.text: The sea is calm, and the Moon hangs over the water. Right now, it is drifting away from you, about three point eight centimeters a year. Tonight, imagine it reverses. It starts coming closer, and it never stops. This is a thought experiment, built from real physics. On average, the Moon is about three hundred eighty-four thousand kilometers away. From the beach, it looks about half a degree wide. About the same size as the Sun. Its light takes about a second and a quarter to reach you. Moonlight is just sunlight, bounced off grey rock. Keep an eye on the number in the corner. It only ever goes down.

Not enough to see on the beach, not yet. The Sun pulls on the tides too, with about half the Moon's effect. But the number keeps falling, and the sea is about to start to move.

And then you look at the Moon again, and it has moved.
